title: NBQ: Next-Best-Question for Dynamic Profiling

problem.claim: Conversational knowledge-discovery settings need a purpose-driven understanding of a person.

contributions.claim: The NBQ framework adaptively selects questions using expected information gain, maintains an updated user state, operates within a turn budget, and produces structured vector-based profiles.
NBQ is instantiated for reciprocal matchmaking by modeling each person through self-description and counterpart-preference representations.
QuickMatch is an approximate-vector-search retrieval layer for reciprocal matching that supports real-time top-match updates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Relative to random or conventional generative questioning baselines, NBQ improves profiling quality by up to 13.6% for AC@T and 14.0% for AR@T.
QuickMatch accelerates retrieval by up to 22.9× while reporting recall of up to 0.989.
QuickMatch provides real-time top-match updates with modest storage overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: Purpose-driven person understanding is needed in conversational knowledge-discovery settings.
NBQ selects the next question by expected information gain and converts adaptive dialogue into a structured profile.
The framework is applied to reciprocal matchmaking using self-description and counterpart-preference vectors.
QuickMatch replaces quadratic pairwise scoring with approximate vector search and supports real-time updates.
The authors report profiling-quality improvements and faster retrieval with high recall.

source_observation.claim: The framework selects questions based on expected information gain and an evolving state of coverage and confidence.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive question selection can allocate limited conversational turns toward information that is most valuable for the stated goal.

application.claim: Use goal-conditioned information gain and an explicit evolving state when designing bounded conversational profiling workflows.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy is optimal beyond the reported settings or metrics.

source_observation.claim: Reciprocal matching is represented through two vectors and scaled with approximate vector search.

interpretation.claim: Separating an entity's attributes from its preferences may support scalable mutual-compatibility retrieval.

application.claim: Model both sides of a compatibility relation explicitly before applying approximate retrieval at scale.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the trade-offs between approximation, recall, storage, and match quality.
